primary_target.fit: The manuscript introduces and tests a general inferential framework for multidimensional ecological support rather than primarily reporting the biological results of one system.

fallback_targets.fit: Strong fit to spatial and temporal ecological patterns and modern methodology, but the manuscript would need to foreground the ecological interpretation of projection through space and time rather than method uptake alone.
Conceptual and methodological scope is compatible, but current empirical evidence spans only a small number of systems and is weaker as a broad-scale macroecological paper than as a methods paper.

title: Beyond flat niche maps: separating added-axis thickness from transferable ecological organization
alternative_titles: Niche thickness is not enough: an information-theoretic test of transferable multidimensional organization
Projection loss and transferability define distinct states of multidimensional niche evidence
From flat maps to ecological state space: separating niche thickness from generalizable organization
one_sentence_claim: Projection loss has at least two empirically separable components: the amount of added-axis state retained after projection and the independent transferability of the organization of that state.
methodological_contribution: conditional added-axis information H(A|B) and effective states exp(H(A|B)) quantify descriptive thickness after declared base state B is known
fitted organization is kept separate from held-out transferability
held-out transferability is scored as E[log P_model(A|B) - log P_model(A)]
prospectively independent groups are scored separately so group mass cannot rescue a conflicting group
estimability under a frozen observation architecture is itself an explicit terminal state
axis semantics, source provenance, frozen decision rules and N2-to-N3 handoff are fail-closed and machine-readable

introduction: flat maps are marginal projections of richer ecological state spaces
added dimensions are often treated as evidence of biological structure without separating magnitude from generalization
state predictions for known-truth and independent empirical tests
results: known-truth benchmark separates thickness, organization and transferability
bat support is vertically thick but non-generalizing
Serengeti support is temporally thick, species-partitioned and generalizing
three empirical states establish separability of inferential layers
discussion: thickness magnitude is not evidence of transferable multidimensional organization
estimability failures should remain scientific outcomes rather than trigger rescue tuning
independent answer checks convert descriptive geometry into a stronger generalization claim
positive temporal organization remains camera-detected local-clock-time organization, not causal displacement or a fundamental niche
cross-system contrast proves existence of distinct states but not why temporal and vertical lanes differ
N2 terminal evidence remains distinct from an N3 axis-resolved state artifact

claim_ceiling: do not claim that temporal dimensions are intrinsically more generalizable than vertical dimensions
do not compare bat and Serengeti information values as controlled effect sizes
do not infer competition or temporal displacement from I(Species;T|Site)
do not relabel camera-detected local clock time as true activity time or solar time
do not relabel height above mean sea level as height above ground
do not treat descriptive thickness alone as transferable multidimensional niche organization
do not promote any terminal summary into an empirical N3 state without an integrity-pinned axis-resolved artifact
do not reopen Tawaki, bat or Serengeti terminal endpoints
